segments.text: Hello has always been how we greet people. Well, not really. Before the telephone, almost nobody said it.
Back then, people said good day, or how do you do. Hello was a shout, to get someone's attention.
Then, in {1876,|eighteen seventy six,} Alexander Graham Bell got the first telephone patent. But there was a problem. What do you say when you pick it up?
Bell had an answer. Ahoy! Like a sailor.
Here's the wild part. His rival, Thomas Edison, had a different idea. In {1877,|eighteen seventy seven,} he wrote that hello was perfect, because it could be heard ten to twenty feet away.
In fact, it caught on so fast that telephone operators got a nickname. The hello girls.
Ahoy lost. Hello won. So every time you answer the phone, you're quoting Edison. Hello, by the way.
